html:
Magadha was a kingdom in the eastern Ganges plain, in what is now southern Bihar in India. It was one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas, and it swallowed the others to become the base of India's first great empires. The map shows it from 500 to 323 BCE, and again in 200 CE for the old Magadha region.

Its strength came from rich rice land, iron from nearby hills, forests full of elephants, and the Ganges for trade. Its kings in turn:

  • Haryanka dynasty: Bimbisara and his son Ajatashatru (500s and 400s BCE) ruled from Rajagriha and conquered Anga and Kosala. Ajatashatru began the fort at Pataliputra, later the capital.
  • Shishunaga dynasty, which took Avanti.
  • Nanda dynasty (about 345 to 322 BCE), rich and feared; its army may have discouraged Alexander's men from marching further east.

The Buddha and Mahavira, founder figure of Jainism, both taught in Magadha, and both Buddhism and Jainism grew there. Around 322 BCE Chandragupta overthrew the Nandas and founded the Maurya Empire, whose core Magadha remained. Later the Gupta Empire also rose from Magadha.
